n_obs = 6,495 two-party voters; n_miss = 1,105 (non-voters, other candidates, ineligible). The Latino shift in this sample is small and imprecise — far from the national exit-poll story. Why? That’s the group task.

title: 4. Project: Did Latino voters pivot to Trump?
text:
Group tasks

Recode team — add generation, income terciles, a strength-of-partisanship measure. Check each against the codebook.
Analysis team — Bayesian logit with brms; predicted probabilities by authoritarianism × Latino × year. Does the gap between reported and intended vote (vote_type) matter?
Shiny team — add a state-by-year panel and a download button.
Skeptics — Is the sample representative of Latino voters? Weighting? Mode? Compare with external estimates.

Each team: branch → commit → pull request.

title: 2. Git workflow
section: Working together (we are all in one repo)
text:
Working together (we are all in one repo)
git pull
git switch -c yourname-topic          # your own branch
# ...edit, add, commit...
git push -u origin yourname-topic
gh pr create --fill                   # open a pull request
Merge on GitHub after a quick review. Then everyone: git switch main && git pull.

title: 2. Git workflow
text:
Rules of the road

Pull before you start; push when you stop.
One person per file at a time where possible (recode vs analysis vs app).
Small commits with clear messages.
Never commit data you weren’t given, passwords, or .Renviron.

title: 2. Git workflow
text:
Merge conflicts
<<<<<<< HEAD
your version
=======
their version
>>>>>>> main
Keep what’s right, delete the markers, then git add + git commit. Or ask the agent: “resolve the merge conflict in R/01_recode.R, keeping both recodes.” — then read its diff.

title: 2. Git workflow
text:
Undo



Situation
Command




Discard edits to a file
git restore file.R


Unstage
git restore --staged file.R


Fix last commit message
git commit --amend (before pushing)


Undo a pushed commit
git revert <hash>

title: 3. Agents: instructions & shortcuts
text:
On start, it loads instruction files: CLAUDE.md (Claude Code), AGENTS.md (Copilot, Codex, Cursor…), .github/copilot-instructions.md (Copilot).
It reads files you mention (@R/01_recode.R) or that it searches for.
It runs commands (R, git) — with your permission.

So the instructions file is the project brief: layout, variable meanings, rules. Here CLAUDE.md is one line — @AGENTS.md — so every tool shares a single source of truth.

title: 3. Agents: instructions & shortcuts
text:
Writing a good AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md

What the project is (one sentence) and the research question.
Where things live; which files are read-only.
Variable definitions and where to cite them (codebook).
Conventions: language, style, where recodes go.
Guardrails: report N and missingness, use weights, don’t push to main.
Keep it short; agents follow concise rules better than essays.

Bootstrap one: run /init in Claude Code, then edit it yourself. Personal, all-project preferences go in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

title: 3. Agents: instructions & shortcuts
text:
Saving credits

/clear between unrelated tasks; long context costs every turn.
Point at files (@R/02_analysis.R) rather than “look around.”
Use plan mode for big changes; approve the plan, then execute.
Smaller model for routine edits.

title: 3. Agents: instructions & shortcuts
text:
Verify, always
Agents produce plausible code. Check variable coding against the codebook, check Ns, and rerun the script yourself.

Goals

Everyone can clone, edit, and push to a shared repo.
Everyone has an AI assistant that knows the project via an instructions file.
We answer one substantive question together — and check the AI’s work.

Slides · Repository

title: 1. Setup
text:
Create an account at https://github.com. Students/faculty: apply for GitHub Education — free Copilot Pro.
Send your username to the instructor to be added as a collaborator (or fork the repo).
Install Git: macOS xcode-select --install; Windows https://git-scm.com.
Identify yourself once:

git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@unm.edu"

Authenticate: install the GitHub CLI and run gh auth login.
